bar.note: iA publishes no latency numbers (only 'boots in a whizz… snappy as jazz'). Bar = best native editors: Sublime 32.5 ms / TextEdit 33.4 ms keyboard-to-photon (Tristan Hume, macOS); internal input→paint ≤5 ms (Typometer, Notepad++ 4.3 ms). Sources in ref/ia/REFERENCE.md.

pieces.title: The page
pieces.judge: the page itself: paper colour, margins, the measure (line length), vertical placement of text in the window, scrolling feel implied by spacing, how the empty space frames the text; overall calm. What the markers are coloured is not this Piece's row: docs/design.md row Markers rests every mark kind at the body's own ink, measured off the Design oracle, so a marker that is quieter on one side than the other is a decision already taken and not a gap. The air above and below a heading is not this Piece's row either: docs/design.md row Block spacing, measured off the Design oracle, costs a blank line one pitch and gives a heading no margin of its own, which is what Quill draws — so the space around a heading is a decision already taken and not a gap. Where the page opens is not this Piece's row: docs/design.md row Page top rests the editor's own page top on a constant 30 logical px, measured off the Design oracle — the 164 device px its first line box stands below the window's top edge, less the 104 px its title bar takes — where the Parity oracle opens two pitches down, 72 px at the default step. So a side whose first line sits higher up the window is a decision already taken and not a gap

pieces.title: The type
pieces.what: Duo / Quattro / Mono, size, line height, rhythm
pieces.judge: the typography only: typeface rendering, size, line height, rhythm, weight and colour of the ink, the spacing of blank lines, how italic/bold sit; would a writer rather read and type in this type. Text size and line pitch are set by a published fourteen-step ladder, one pitch per step (docs/design.md, rows Text sizes and Line pitch), so the gap to name is a pitch or a size that misses its own step, not a pitch you would have set differently. Where a state is a crop of the text column rather than a whole window, judge the type inside the crop. What the markers are coloured is not this Piece's row: docs/design.md row Markers rests every mark kind at the body's own ink, measured off the Design oracle, so a marker that is quieter on one side than the other is a decision already taken and not a gap. Block spacing is settled the same way — docs/design.md row Block spacing, measured off the Design oracle, rests a blank line at one pitch and gives a heading no margin of its own — so the gap to name is a blank line that is not one pitch, not air above a heading you would have set differently. Where the page opens is not this Piece's row: docs/design.md row Page top rests the editor's own page top on a constant 30 logical px, measured off the Design oracle — the 164 device px its first line box stands below the window's top edge, less the 104 px its title bar takes — where the Parity oracle opens two pitches down, 72 px at the default step. So a side whose first line sits higher up the window is a decision already taken and not a gap

What the markers are coloured is not this Piece's row: docs/design.md row Markers rests every mark kind at the body's own ink, measured off the Design oracle, so a marker that is quieter on one side than the other is a decision already taken and not a gap. Nor is how far a selection reaches: docs/design.md rows Selection, Held newline and Multi-row fill make a selection a fill of the text container, so a row the selection runs past is filled to the container's right edge and a row it entered from above starts at the container's left, gutter and all, and only the anchor and the focus are measured off glyphs — a band wider than the words beneath it is that rule and not a gap. The air above and below a heading is not this Piece's row either: docs/design.md row Block spacing, measured off the Design oracle, costs a blank line one pitch and gives a heading no margin of its own, which is what Quill draws — so the space around a heading is a decision already taken and not a gap. So a side whose first line sits higher up the window is a decision already taken and not a gap

pieces.title: Focus & typewriter
pieces.judge: focus mode and typewriter scrolling: how the non-focused text is dimmed (colour, amount), sentence vs paragraph scope, where the active line rests in the window, whether the eye is drawn to exactly the right place. Three things here are decisions already taken and not gaps. How many dim tiers there are: docs/design.md row Dim tiers gives Focus two tiers, bright and dim, with one dim per theme that Sentence and Paragraph share, measured off the Design oracle (ADR 0015 supersedes ADR 0006's near tier), so a side holding a third shade between the lit sentence and the dim is showing a tier this app does not have. What the markers are coloured: docs/design.md row Markers rests every mark kind at the body's own ink, also measured off the Design oracle, so a marker that is quieter on one side than the other is a decision already taken. And where the page is scrolled to in the dark-sentence-typewriter state: Typewriter holds the caret's line at the window's vertical centre (docs/design.md row Typewriter) and ours has not been built to (#115), so the line resting somewhere else down the window is a Piece not yet ported rather than a dimming that reads wrong. The air above and below a heading is not this Piece's row either: docs/design.md row Block spacing, measured off the Design oracle, costs a blank line one pitch and gives a heading no margin of its own, which is what Quill draws — so the space around a heading is a decision already taken and not a gap. So a side whose first line sits higher up the window is a decision already taken and not a gap

pieces.title: Dark & light
pieces.judge: the two palettes: paper and ink colours, contrast, how the markers read against the words, whether the ground feels designed rather than inverted. The light and dark states are a crop of the Design oracle at a passage carrying every mark kind, so what is in front of you is the page itself and none of the furniture around it: judge the paper, the ink on it, and how the `>`, the `-`, the `1.` and the task box sit against the words they mark. A marker that reads as loud as its words is the answer here rather than a defect — the Design oracle rests every mark kind at the body's own ink (docs/design.md row Markers), and a quieted marker on either side is the gap. The air above and below a heading is not this Piece's row either: docs/design.md row Block spacing, measured off the Design oracle, costs a blank line one pitch and gives a heading no margin of its own, which is what Quill draws — so the space around a heading is a decision already taken and not a gap. At dark-bars the pair is two whole windows on the dark ground rather than a crop of the page, so the title bar and the stats bar are in it. Their type is Adwaita Sans, the GNOME UI face, and the oracle's frozen shot fell through the same font stack to Liberation Sans on the machine that froze it, so a run of chrome text a few pixels wider or narrower on one side is the two faces and not a gap; the title reads the Document's file name, which is what the bar is for. Paper, ink, the dim tier, the accent and both selection fills are docs/design.md's rows (Paper · ink · dim, Accent, Active fill, Idle fill), measured off the Design oracle, so one of those colours differing from the oracle in front of you is a decision already taken and not a gap. Nor is the type at that state: the size and the line pitch are a published fourteen-step ladder's (rows Text sizes and Line pitch), one pitch per step, so leading that is a little tighter or looser on one side is that ladder and not a gap. Where the page opens is not this Piece's row: docs/design.md row Page top rests the editor's own page top on a constant 30 logical px, measured off the Design oracle — the 164 device px its first line box stands below the window's top edge, less the 104 px its title bar takes — where the Parity oracle opens two pitches down, 72 px at the default step. So a side whose first line sits higher up the window is a decision already taken and not a gap

pieces.title: Markup rendering
pieces.what: Headings, emphasis, lists, quotes, code, links in the editor
pieces.judge: how Markdown is shown while writing: heading markers, emphasis, lists, blockquotes, code, links — are markers quiet, does the text stay readable, do headings and structure read at a glance without the text jumping. All three states are the hanging-marker gutter and the body column: gutters is the six heading levels, whose `#` runs step out into the left gutter by level + 1 cells so their words all land on the body column and `###### ` reaches the container's own left edge; blocks is that deepest heading above a quote, a bullet and an ordinal, whose markers stand on the body column instead and push their own words inward, with no rule beside the quote; wrapped is a bullet, a three-digit ordinal and a quote each long enough to wrap, so the rows under the first are what there is to read. Judge where each row starts and how the columns read together. What a wrapped item's rows do is docs/design.md row What hangs, measured off the Design oracle: an item's continuation rows hang in under its own first word, by that item's own marker run — two cells for `- ` and `> `, five for `123. ` — and a wrapped quote carries no second `>`, so a continuation that returns to the body column is a fault and one that repeats the marker is another. What the markers are coloured is not this Piece's row: docs/design.md row Markers rests every mark kind at the body's own ink, measured off the Design oracle, so a marker that is quieter on one side than the other is a decision already taken and not a gap. Where the page opens is not this Piece's row: docs/design.md row Page top rests the editor's own page top on a constant 30 logical px, measured off the Design oracle — the 164 device px its first line box stands below the window's top edge, less the 104 px its title bar takes — where the Parity oracle opens two pitches down, 72 px at the default step. So a side whose first line sits higher up the window is a decision already taken and not a gap

pieces.title: Chrome & menus
pieces.what: Bars, counters, palette, what hides while typing, the empty state
pieces.judge: the chrome: what UI is visible around the text, the stats/word-count bar, title, menus/palette, how it recedes while writing; is there exactly as much interface as a writer needs and no more. At bars and empty the comparison is the two bars themselves: a 32 px title bar with a Library toggle at its left, the Document's name centred and a View button at its right, a 26 px stats bar reading words, characters and reading time with the number stronger than its label, the hairline rule that stands between a bar and a page continuing past it, and the greys and the type size the two are set in. The title reads the Document's file name without its extension (sample for a shot of ref/sample.md, Untitled until the first save), which is what the bar is for and not a gap. The bars' type is set in Adwaita Sans, the GNOME UI face and the counterpart of the SF Pro Text the Design oracle sets its chrome in; the Parity oracle's frozen shots fell through the same font stack to Liberation Sans on the machine that froze them, so a run of chrome text that is a few pixels wider or narrower on one side is the two faces and not a gap — the greys, the size and the weight step between a number and its label are what to compare. An empty Document shows "Start writing…" on its first line in the grey Focus dims prose to, and nothing else on the page. At typing the chrome has stepped back — title bar gone, stats bar dimmed to about a third — and the page under it is unchanged. At view-menu the View menu is open under the View button with its first row selected, and the comparison is the menu's typography, its spacing, its ticks and its key labels, not its row count: the native menu carries more rows than the oracle's by design (docs/shortcuts.md § View menu lists every feature the port will have, and a row whose feature is not built yet is greyed with its chord), so a longer menu is a decision already taken and not a gap. At palette the Palette is open over the page from Ctrl+K: a panel a third of the way down the window with a search field, a hairline, section headings in small capitals and 24 px rows with the chord at the right, the first row selected in the accent; the comparison is the panel's proportions, its type sizes, its greys and its selected row, not the wording or the number of its rows, which are the registry's (docs/shortcuts.md) and carry every Command the port will have, a row not built yet greyed. What the markers are coloured is not this Piece's row: docs/design.md row Markers rests every mark kind at the body's own ink, measured off the Design oracle, so a marker that is quieter on one side than the other is a decision already taken and not a gap. The air above and below a heading is not this Piece's row either: docs/design.md row Block spacing, measured off the Design oracle, costs a blank line one pitch and gives a heading no margin of its own, which is what Quill draws — so the space around a heading is a decision already taken and not a gap. Where the page opens is not this Piece's row: docs/design.md row Page top rests the editor's own page top on a constant 30 logical px, measured off the Design oracle — the 164 device px its first line box stands below the window's top edge, less the 104 px its title bar takes — where the Parity oracle opens two pitches down, 72 px at the default step. So a side whose first line sits higher up the window is a decision already taken and not a gap

pieces.title: File handling
pieces.judge: file handling UI: the library/sidebar, file list, how documents are named and found, open/save affordances, how it looks next to the editor; would a writer trust it with their manuscripts. What the markers are coloured is not this Piece's row: docs/design.md row Markers rests every mark kind at the body's own ink, measured off the Design oracle, so a marker that is quieter on one side than the other is a decision already taken and not a gap. The air above and below a heading is not this Piece's row either: docs/design.md row Block spacing, measured off the Design oracle, costs a blank line one pitch and gives a heading no margin of its own, which is what Quill draws — so the space around a heading is a decision already taken and not a gap At library the comparison is the pane beside the page: a 368 px column on the theme's paper with a hairline down its right edge, a search field at the top, a sort control and a count under it, the rows themselves — a document mark, the name, the date it was last written and two lines of what it says — and the status line at its foot. Four of those rows are decisions already taken and not gaps. A row shows the name without its extension, which is what the Library spec asks for (`library.show_extensions` is false by default), so `sea-storm` against the oracle's `sea-storm.md` is the setting and not a gap. The pane is headed by one section per Location, named for that folder, where the oracle has one browser Location it heads “Library”. Folders stand before the files, which is the order the spec sorts a section in, and a folder is closed until it is opened, so the oracle's Drafts standing open with its two documents beneath it against ours standing closed is the spec's “collapsed” and not a gap. And the pane is set in Adwaita Sans, the GNOME UI face, where the oracle sets its Library in iA Writer Quattro and its frozen shots fell through to Liberation Sans — the spec puts the sidebar in the UI font, so a run of text a few pixels wider or narrower on one side is the two faces and not a gap; the greys, the sizes and the spacing are what to compare. At search the query is in the field and the list is not narrowed by it yet: searching is the next ticket's and is unbuilt, so that state is not this round's to win. Where the page opens is not this Piece's row: docs/design.md row Page top rests the editor's own page top on a constant 30 logical px, measured off the Design oracle — the 164 device px its first line box stands below the window's top edge, less the 104 px its title bar takes — where the Parity oracle opens two pitches down, 72 px at the default step. So a side whose first line sits higher up the window is a decision already taken and not a gap

pieces.title: Live rendering
pieces.what: Markup folded away in place, headings on the ladder, furniture in the marker cells
pieces.judge: the page with Live on: whether the markup reads as a rendered page while it is still the source — the markers gone from every block but the one the caret is in, that block showing its source to edit, the headings larger by level, and the words landing on the same body column folded or not. The one state is asserted rather than paired (ADR 0017): neither oracle holds it, so tools/assert-state.mjs measures it off ours own pixels and the Piece takes that answer.

pieces.title: Preview
pieces.what: The rendered page beside the Editor, and in place of it
pieces.judge: nothing, and no critic is spent here: every state of this Piece names `assert`, so it is measured off ours' own pixels by tools/assert-state.mjs and shown to nobody (ADR 0017). Neither oracle holds the Preview — legacy/ shows Markdown as source and has no rendered page at all, and iA Writer for Mac's own preview is that app's design rather than this one's, which is why #263 puts Preview outside ADR 0015's reach — so the states are won on arithmetic instead: in Split, the divider at half the window with the Editor's paper one side of it and the Template's the other, and the heading at the top of the rendered page centred in the pane it is drawn in; in Full, one paper across the whole window and that heading centred in the window itself. What a still cannot hold — the refresh, the scroll sync, a link opening — is the feature's Hand test.

pieces.title: Export
pieces.what: The Export dialog over the page, and the file it writes
pieces.judge: nothing, and no critic is spent here either: the one state names `assert`, so it is measured off ours' own pixels by tools/assert-state.mjs and shown to nobody (ADR 0017). Neither oracle holds an Export dialog — legacy/ has none at all, and iA Writer for Mac's own is that app's dialog rather than this one's — so the state is won on arithmetic instead: the dialog standing over the page as a second ground, inside the window and centred on it, its Options expander open, and the file name seeded from the Document's own name. What a still cannot hold — the file that is written, the printer, the notification and the clipboard — is the feature's Hand test.

pieces.title: Syntax highlight
pieces.what: English words coloured by Category, with Focus and Live precedence
pieces.judge: the five Category colours and which words carry them: is the noun red the oracle's red and the verb blue its blue, and does the same word take the same colour on both sides. Three states are crops of the Design oracle at ref/ia/mac-native/passage-syntax.md — all five Categories on each ground, and all five under Focus Sentence — so what is in front of you is the page itself and none of the furniture around it. The colours are docs/design.md row Syntax colours, measured off iA Writer for Mac on both grounds, so a Category reading a different hue or a different depth of colour on one side is a gap. So is a word split differently: docs/design.md row What a contraction colours puts `ca` and `n't` in different colours, `well` and `known` in different colours with the hyphen between them plain, and a possessive `'s` plain after its noun while the `'s` of `it's` is a verb — a side that paints a whole hyphenated compound one colour, or leaves an `n't` in the body's ink, is showing that row broken. At focus-sentence the dimmed rows carry no Category colour at all, one grey (docs/design.md row Dim over a Category), so a dimmed row holding a faint red is a gap and a dimmed row holding one flat grey is the row working. Four things are decisions already taken and not gaps. **Which Category a word is given**: that is the shipped tagger's answer and not this app's design. #310 § Out of Scope puts retraining or fine-tuning the tagger outside this work, and § Accuracy acceptance bounds it instead with a test — quill-engine/tests/syntax_accuracy.rs scores the shipped model against iA's own stills word by word and fails the build under 86 %; it stands at 89.3 %. So a word one side calls a noun and the other a verb, or colours where the other leaves it plain, is that bound and not a gap, however plainly wrong it looks: the two apps run different taggers on purpose. What is a gap is a colour, a dim or a split that differs — the things the rows above decide. The typeface: the Design oracle is set in Mono throughout (ref/ia/mac-native/NOTES.md § The rig, which fits a cell grid Duo cannot), and ours is Duo, the port's default and the type Piece's own row — so glyph shapes, letter advances, cap heights and a line pitch one pixel apart are the two faces and the type ladder (docs/design.md rows Text sizes and Line pitch), not a gap. The caret: at focus-sentence both sides stand one after `more`, and what it is made of is the caret Piece's rows — Caret column, Caret width and Accent, which rests it at #00bfff on both grounds — so a bar that is a different blue, a different width or a different height is a decision already taken. The two all-Category states carry no bar on either side, which is the capture, not a caret that failed to draw. And where the page opens: docs/design.md row Page top rests the editor's own page top on a constant 30 logical px, so air above the first line that differs between two crops is the framing. The other two states are asserted under ADR 0017 and no critic is spent on them: no mac-native frame holds two Categories together and none holds Live at all, so adjectives-adverbs and live are measured off ours' own pixels. tools/assert-state.mjs measures expected and absent Role ink, preserved glyph coverage, colour inside the bright sentence rows, and colour on the scaled Live heading. Settings persistence and typing remain the feature Hand test.

pieces.title: Style check
pieces.what: Fillers, redundancies and clichés struck through on the prose stream
pieces.judge: nothing, and no critic is spent here either: all nine states name `assert`, so each is measured off ours' own pixels by tools/assert-state.mjs and shown to nobody (ADR 0017). legacy/ has no Style check at all, so the Parity oracle cannot hold one of them, and the capture that would give the Design oracle its say — #354 — has not landed, so the mark is provisional and docs/design.md carries no Style row yet. What the nine are won on instead is arithmetic over the same page shot `--style off`, where the marks are the only thing that differs: thirteen of them with every List on ref/style.md and six with Fillers alone, which is the matcher's answer arriving on the page; each a thin rule lying along a line of prose over columns that line has ink in, with nothing changed outside the text column; and each drawn in an ink of the line it lies on, which is what the strike taking the word's own colour comes to — dimmed with its word at focus-light and focus-dark, in the Category colours at syntax-light and syntax-dark, standing over the selection fill at select-light and select-dark, and in the dark ground's ink on the dark. Which phrase belongs to which List is not a thing the pixels can say, because all three Lists draw the same mark by design (#356 § The mark); that is held by quill-engine/tests/style_fixture.rs, which names every phrase of the passage by byte range and List, and by the count under `--style fillers`. When #354 lands the nine take mac-native crops as opponents one for one and become judged. The toggles, the Settings rows, typing and persistence are the feature's Hand test.

log.msg: Harness up: headless Chromium screenshots, latency bench, blind A/B pairing. Core editor engine written (textarea + mirror, incremental line render, custom caret, focus/typewriter, markdown tokenizer).

Reference package in: 49 real iA Writer screenshots (App Store, MS Store, ia.net) with verbatim transcriptions, Duo/Quattro/Mono fonts (OFL) with parsed metrics, measured spec sheet (paper #f9f9f9 / #1a1a1a, ink #1c1c1c / #cccccc, caret #00b5ff ≈0.15 em wide, line pitch ≈1.7×, 64-char measure, hanging # markers), latency bar from third-party measurements.

All nine pieces picked blind. Latency won on round 4: app-internal 2.43 ms mean / 15.61 ms worst (bar ≤5/≤16), real keys via /dev/uinput → presented frame 12.17 ms, caret settles 8.1 ms after the key (was 57 ms), cold launch to first document frame 370 ms. Final integration smoke passed in all three fonts and both themes.
